risk_flags.clause: The Lessee shall pay a security deposit of ₹2,50,000 and the deposit shall be forfeited in full if the Lessee vacates before the lock-in period.
risk_flags.reason: The clause forfeits the entire deposit on early exit regardless of actual loss - a punitive pattern.
risk_flags.law_reference: Delhi Rent Control Act deposit rules

risk_flags.clause: A late fee of ₹2,000 per day shall apply for delayed rent after the due date.
risk_flags.reason: The late fee accrues per day, which compounds quickly and is a classic unenforceable-penalty pattern.
risk_flags.law_reference: Delhi Rent Control Act notice requirements

risk_flags.clause: The Lessor or his agents may enter the premises without prior notice at any time to inspect the property.
risk_flags.reason: The entry clause lets the landlord enter without effective notice limits, violating standard notice requirements.
risk_flags.law_reference: Delhi Rent Control Act notice requirements

risk_flags.clause: The Lessor may evict the Lessee for any reason with 48 hours notice.
risk_flags.reason: The termination/eviction clause is one-sided: termination at will/sole discretion; only 2.0 days notice (minimum here: 15).

risk_flags.clause: The Lessee waives all rights under the Delhi Rent Control Act and any other tenant protection law.
risk_flags.reason: The tenant is made to waive legal rights or protections; such blanket waivers are typically unenforceable but signal intent.
risk_flags.law_reference: Delhi Rent Control Act notice requirements

risk_flags.clause: The Lessee shall be responsible for all repairs including structural and major repairs to the premises.
risk_flags.reason: Structural/major repair obligations are shifted to the tenant; these are legally the landlord's responsibility.
risk_flags.law_reference: Delhi Rent Control Act notice requirements

risk_flags.clause: No guest shall stay overnight in the premises without the prior written permission of the Lessor.
risk_flags.reason: The guest policy is unusually restrictive (blanket bans or per-stay landlord permission) and intrudes on ordinary quiet enjoyment.
risk_flags.law_reference: Delhi Rent Control Act notice requirements

risk_flags.clause: The Lessee shall not approach any government authority with any complaint regarding the premises or this agreement.
risk_flags.reason: The clause punishes lawful complaints to authorities - retaliatory and almost certainly unenforceable, and a serious red flag about the landlord.
risk_flags.law_reference: Delhi Rent Control Act notice requirements

risk_flags.clause: The agreement shall renew only at the sole discretion of the Lessor with 60 days notice from the Lessee required for renewal.
risk_flags.reason: Renewal (or renewal rent) is at the landlord's sole discretion - the tenant has no predictable right to stay.
risk_flags.law_reference: Delhi Rent Control Act notice requirements

summary: This lease contains several clauses that appear one-sided or potentially unlawful. The strongest concerns are around fees, notice rights, eviction, and repair obligations, and those terms should be revised before signing.
sentences: This Rent Agreement is executed at New Delhi between Shri Ramesh Kumar (Lessor) and Ms.
Priya Sharma (Lessee) for the residential premises situated at C-14, Lajpat Nagar, New Delhi.
The monthly rent shall be ₹25,000 payable in advance on or before the 5th day of each English calendar month.
The Lessee shall pay a security deposit of ₹2,50,000 and the deposit shall be forfeited in full if the Lessee vacates before the lock-in period.
A late fee of ₹2,000 per day shall apply for delayed rent after the due date.
The Lessor or his agents may enter the premises without prior notice at any time to inspect the property.
The Lessor may evict the Lessee for any reason with 48 hours notice.
The Lessee waives all rights under the Delhi Rent Control Act and any other tenant protection law.
The Lessee shall be responsible for all repairs including structural and major repairs to the premises.
No guest shall stay overnight in the premises without the prior written permission of the Lessor.
The Lessee shall not approach any government authority with any complaint regarding the premises or this agreement.
The agreement shall renew only at the sole discretion of the Lessor with 60 days notice from the Lessee required for renewal.
